note.saw: A blank canvas and the brief: a pufferfish in the super-geometric style, with reference images of rainbow mandalas and tunnels of cubes.
note.changing: The first full build: the puffer's ball made as a real 3D faceted sphere where every facet is a tiny jewel pyramid, true 3D spikes for spines, five spinning rings of petals behind it, a tunnel of cubes filling the corners, a ring of runes and the name on a geometric band at the bottom.
note.why: The super-geometric style gets its intensity from repetition and density, so the fish itself had to be made of geometry, not just decorated with it.
note.idea: An inflated pufferfish built as a genuine three-dimensional star-cut sphere, every facet a small jewel pyramid and every spine a real spike, floating in a spinning chrysanthemum of petal rings with a tunnel of cubes far behind.

note.saw: The ball looked like a rainbow beach ball, the spines were a dull grey, and the tail melted into the petals behind it.
note.changing: Wraps the ball, tail and fins in one glowing cream and cyan outline, cuts the facets finer so they sparkle, recolours the spines gold and magenta, and tries new lancet and rounded petal shapes so the rings are not all the same gem.
note.why: A hero needs a silhouette you can read from across the room.

note.saw: The inner petal rings hid the alien faces in the outer rings, and the green eye on a teal head had too little contrast to stand out.
note.changing: Re-spaces the rings so the eyes and faces show, enlarges the little star-cut orbs among the petals, and turns the eye into a hot magenta and orange vortex portal.
note.why: In a DMT space the beings should be looking back at you, so they have to be visible, and the eye becomes the one place your gaze lands first.

note.saw: The ball still read as horizontal stripes of colour, not as a solid shape.
note.changing: Lays gold seams along the edges of the hidden twenty-sided solid inside the sphere, with star jewels at its twelve corners, and adds sparkles at the petal tips.
note.why: Showing the skeleton of the solid makes the word Polyhedron literal, and the sparkles bring in light.

note.saw: The belly facets went a muddy olive grey, the name band was plain, and the string-art veil behind the petals looked fuzzy up close.
note.changing: Fills the name band with a faint honeycomb, caps its ends with star-cut orb jewels, sharpens the string-art veil into crisp hairlines, and tries a cool cyan bounce light on the belly.
note.why: Every surface in hyperspace is covered in living ornament, even the sign.

note.saw: The cyan bounce light turned the shadows on the belly a washed-out grey tan.
note.changing: Shifts the shading so shadows swing toward magenta and ultraviolet instead of black, with a hot pink light bouncing up from below; the belly now glows peach, pink and orange.
note.why: Visionary art never goes muddy; even its shadows glow.

note.saw: The cubes in the corners were plain, and the flower had no big straight lines holding it together.
note.changing: Puts eyes in the walls of the cube tunnel, as in one of the reference images, stretches a six-pointed star and a twelve-pointed star across the petal rings, and thickens the fish's outline.
note.why: Eyes in the walls are the classic something-is-watching moment, and the big stars give the flower a sacred-geometry frame.

note.saw: The upper ring was still a tangle of crossing lines at close range, with the string-art veil drawn over the petals.
note.changing: Moves the string art behind every petal ring so it only shimmers through the gaps, and pulls the lettering in from the rim.
note.why: Crisp geometry needs breathing room, and a veil reads best when you see it through gaps.

note.saw: SavesFish asked for the name to be very legible, and this one was small, striped and crowded near the rim.
note.changing: Splits the name into SAVES on a band at the top and FISH on a band at the bottom, in tall solid cream capitals with a gold edge and a thick dark outline, and centres the puffer in the badge.
note.why: SavesFish liked split capitals on another piece, and two arcs give the badge a calm, symmetrical frame.

note.saw: The dark halo behind the letters spilled past the bands and muddied their sawtooth trim.
note.changing: Slims the halo so the teeth and gold borders are crisp again, and checks that the name still reads at small size.
note.why: Legibility first, then ornament around it.

note.saw: Looking fresh at the first artist's final: the flower was a jumble of five similar rings with every petal cycling the whole rainbow, the puffer read as a disco ball with random shard-like spines and a tiny pink box for a mouth, nothing glowed, and the bands and corners were flat.
note.changing: Rebuilds the picture around three interleaved rings with clear jobs, magenta lancets with eyes in front, cyan cut gems with alien faces behind and thin spikes between, each petal outlined with line-gap-line contour bands and a darker jewel half; the fish gets an ultraviolet back fading to a gold belly, hexagonal eye-spots and a light glowing behind it.
note.why: A mandala hits hardest when your eye can count its rings; the density then lives inside each ring.
note.idea: Keep what works, the true 3D jewel puffer and the split SAVES / FISH name, and give everything else a hierarchy: fewer, bolder rings each with its own colour family, a fish whose species reads from its face and crown of spines, a real light source behind it, and crafted bands instead of flat ones.

note.saw: The new halo was huge and white and bleached the nearby petals pink, the petal centres were flat, and the mouth looked like a mailbox.
note.changing: Moves the big glow behind the petals so it shines through the gaps, cuts the petal centres into faceted jewels, and fills the corners with a spiral tunnel built from one detailed cube, with an eye or a tiny cube in its face, repeated hundreds of times.
note.why: Light from behind makes the flower look backlit, like stained glass, instead of washed out.

note.saw: The spines on the front of the body lay across the belly like scattered shards, and the eye-spots on the back read as black holes.
note.changing: Keeps long, even spines only around the silhouette and turns the front ones into short star studs, redraws the spots as nested rainbow hexagon eyes, and joins the mouth into the glowing outline as a snout with octagonal pouty lips.
note.why: A crown of rays around a clean jewel reads as porcupine puffer instantly and stays geometric.

note.saw: The zone between the spine tips and the name bands was pale and empty, and the bands themselves were flat navy.
note.changing: Circles the fish with a black ring of 48 tiny eyes, adds a magenta echo outline to the letters, and dresses the bands with ultraviolet facets, rows of beads and a triangle border.
note.why: The fish now sits inside a watching portal, and its tail breaking out of the ring gives depth.

note.saw: The glow inside the eye ring was a pale wash, so the cream spines lost contrast, and the petal centres were still plain up close.
note.changing: Deepens the glow to a saturated cyan, stitches string art into every petal centre, enlarges the alien faces, and gives the eye ring a crown of 96 tiny teeth.
note.why: String art makes curves out of straight lines, which is exactly the super-geometric way to add softness.

note.saw: At badge size the outer petals read as a muted purple grey.
note.changing: Adds a neon bloom under the petal edges, pink under the lancets and cyan under the gems, brightens the jewel centres, lightens the shadowed halves, and sets tiny star-cut orbs at the lancet tips.
note.why: The puffer's orb now repeats at three sizes, the self-similar echo that makes a DMT image feel fractal.

note.saw: The mouth was the right shape but too small to read at badge size.
note.changing: Scales the mouth up as part of the silhouette, enlarges the side fin with a gold gill arc behind it, and adds four-pointed star glints on the lit side of the ball.
note.why: The pout is what makes a puffer a puffer.

note.saw: Each ring only alternated between two colour schemes, so the flower felt static.
note.changing: Gives each ring eight colour schemes walking in order around a rainbow wheel, while the outer bands stay fixed as magenta lancets and cyan gems.
note.why: An ordered spectrum makes the chrysanthemum seem to spin, like the rainbow contour bands in one of the reference images.

note.saw: The warm gem centres, darkened toward black, had gone olive brown.
note.changing: Darkens them with the same colour-shifted jewel shadow as the belly, sliding toward violet instead of black.
note.why: Same rule as the belly: in this world nothing turns to mud.

note.saw: The portal eye pulled you in and then stopped at a flat bullseye, and the cyan glow around the spine crown felt like soft fog in a world made of crystal.
note.changing: Opens the pupil into a tunnel of ten turning hexagons that falls to a tiny star-cut orb, turns every eye in the ring and the petals toward it, strings a faint star net of hairlines between the spine tips, and lets a curl of seven rune glyphs pour from the lips.
note.why: Recursion is the breakthrough itself, the fish inside the eye of the fish, and a room full of eyes all looking at one thing is the uncanny DMT moment; the net gives the glow a crystal skeleton and the glyphs let the fish speak the language of the rim.
note.visionary: Takes all four of the Visionary's first suggestions, each kept faint enough to protect the hierarchy.

note.saw: The tunnel pupil, the gazing eyes and the star net all worked, but the dark discs behind the glyphs read as a column of black beads beside the mouth.
note.changing: Drops the discs and draws the glyphs as gold and cyan strokes on a thin dark underlay, larger at the lips and shrinking along the curl.
note.why: Visible language should look like light being spoken, not like holes punched in the glow.
note.visionary: Keeps the Visionary's speaking glyphs but redraws them so they read as light.

note.saw: The ball's skin was still holding its breath, the tail looked parked rather than swimming, and the corners of the square were static.
note.changing: Makes the small light triangle in every facet swell and shrink with distance from the portal eye so ripples roll across the body, trails three fading afterimages of the tail's rim in violet, magenta and cyan, and turns two rings of corner cubes inside out, dark on top and lit on the sides.
note.why: In hyperspace surfaces breathe and time smears into geometry; the ripple ties the eye to the body, the trails make the fish swim through the flower, and the flipped cubes pull your eye back to the centre.
note.visionary: Takes all three of the Visionary's second suggestions.

note.saw: The facet ripple worked as a quiet shimmer rolling out from the eye, but the first tail afterimage hid under the tail's thick glowing outline and the other two were too faint to read as motion.
note.changing: Pushes the three afterimages further out from the tail fan and makes them a little stronger.
note.why: An afterimage only reads as movement if you can see the gap between the thing and its echo.
note.visionary: Tunes the Visionary's tail trails, which sat too close and too faint on the first try.

visions.seen: The puffer is a jeweled geodesic sun swelling in a chrysanthemum of watching gems, and its portal eye is pulling me in. But when I get there the pupil just stops at a flat bullseye, and the cyan haze around the spine crown feels soft, like airbrushed fog in a world made of crystal.
suggestions: The portal eye, upper right of the ball (about 478,343 in the 800 box): what if the pupil opened into a Droste tunnel? Six or seven nested hexagons, each turned 7 to 8 degrees from the one outside it and alternating ultraviolet and cyan, shrinking to a white pinpoint, with a tiny stellated orb in the center (your puffer motif at a fourth scale, the fish inside the eye of the fish). Reuse the orb with a scaled `<use>`. Why DMT: recursion is the breakthrough itself. The eye stops being a target and becomes the vanishing point of the whole badge.

Every eye in the mandala, meaning the 48 tiny eyes on the black ring around the fish and the big lancet eyes in the petal field: I see their pupils turning toward the portal eye. Shift each pupil 1 to 1.5 px (2 to 3 px on the big lancet eyes) along the vector toward 478,343. Why DMT: the uncanny moment when every entity in the room is looking at the same thing. It also steers the viewer's gaze to the face without making anything bigger.

The cyan glow between the spine tips and the black eye ring (radius about 205 to 225 from the center): stretch a star-polygon net across it. Connect each spine tip to the tip 5 to 7 places around with 0.6 px hairlines in pale cyan and white at about 35% opacity, drawn behind the spines. Why DMT: it gives the haze a crystal skeleton and makes "Polyhedron" literal, as if the spines are holding a hyperdimensional shape open. It echoes your curve-stitched petal cores, and at that faintness the cream crown still pops.

Just right of the pink lips, mouth on the right side (about 560 to 620, 425): a short curling stream of 6 or 7 glyphs from the rune ring's own alphabet, gold and cyan, pouring out of the mouth and shrinking as they curve toward the eye ring at 3 o'clock. Keep them outside the silhouette. Why DMT: the entities speak in visible language. The fish is literally speaking the ring, and the mouth reads louder at badge size without being made bigger.
visions.keep: The SAVES / FISH split capitals on calm navy cartouches with the magenta echo and gold edge (instant at 240 px, so let nothing touch them). The countershaded ball, ultraviolet back to gold belly. The cream and gold spine crown against saturated cyan. The orb motif at three scales. The neon-bloomed chrysanthemum of alien-faced gems and eyed lancets. The eye-filled cube-tunnel corners. And the rainbow tail breaking out of the ring.

visions.seen: You took all four and the eye has opened: I fall through ten turning hexagons and land on a little fish waiting at the bottom, while every eye in the room turns to watch me go. The rune glyphs bubble out of the lips like the fish is singing the rim. Now the ball's skin is the one thing still holding its breath.
suggestions: The geodesic skin of the ball, all over: what if the light inset triangle inside each facet swelled and shrank with distance from the portal eye (about 478,343)? Something like inset scale = 0.35 + 0.25 * sin(d / 14), where d is the distance from the facet's center to the eye. Concentric halftone ripples would roll out from the eye across the whole puffer. Leave the facet hues and the ultraviolet-to-gold countershading exactly as they are; only the inset size changes. Why DMT: in hyperspace surfaces breathe, and the eye sends a pulse through the body, tying the two biggest shapes into one living system. At badge size it reads as a shimmer, not as clutter.

The petal field just left of the rainbow tail, at 9 o'clock (about x 60 to 115, y 300 to 490): I see three tracers of the tail's outer edge. Stepped copies of the fan's zigzag rim, each about 9 px further out and turned 3 degrees, drawn as 2 px bands in violet, magenta, then cyan at about 70, 45 and 25% opacity, each with a 0.6 px black keyline so it holds against the petals. Stop them short of the rune ring. Why DMT: tracers are time smearing into geometry. The fish is swimming through the flower, and the tail breaking out of the ring looks even more like it is moving.

The cube-tunnel corners, which only show in the square render (the round badge crops them): a Necker ripple. In two concentric bands around the center (distance about 450 to 480 and 530 to 560 from 400,400), shade each cube so it reads as a hollow room corner instead of a block: make the flat diamond face the darkest, light the side faces, and keep each eye where it sits. Why DMT: space flips inside out, and the rings of reversed cubes spread out from the badge like dimensions rippling, which pulls the eye back toward the center.
visions.keep: The Droste pupil with the fish at its bottom, the pupils all turned toward it, the faint star net strung between the spine tips, and the glyph stream from the lips. All four landed and none of them crowds the face. Keep the SAVES / FISH split capitals on calm navy cartouches, untouched by any pattern. Keep the countershaded ball, the cream and gold spine crown on saturated cyan, the orb repeated at three scales, the neon chrysanthemum of eyed lancets and alien gems, and the rainbow tail breaking out of the ring.

visions.seen: The tracers caught up: three zigzag ghosts trail the tail through the petals, so the fish is really swimming through the flower now, and the skin hums a quiet halftone pulse outward from the eye. But the spines are still flat paper cutouts and the snout is a smooth peach box, the only soft, ordinary things on a body made of cut jewel.
suggestions: The spine crown, all the way around the ball (every cream and gold spike from the crest down to the long teeth under the belly): I see each spine cut along its length into two facets, like a crystal shard. Split each triangle on the line from the middle of its base to its tip. The half whose edge faces the upper left (where the sparkles say the light comes from) takes its current fill lifted about 15% toward warm white. The other half takes it pushed toward hot amber-rose, hue-shifted toward magenta and never brown, with a 0.5 px dark ridge line down the middle. Keep the black outline and the cyan bead at each tip. Why DMT: in hyperspace nothing is flat and every edge catches light. The crown stops being a ring of paper and becomes a corona of prisms that matches the pyramid skin. At badge size it reads as sparkle and depth, and the cream and gold still sit on the cyan.

The snout, the peach box just left of the pink gem lips (about x 520 to 558, y 398 to 448): what if it were cut like the skin? Four triangular facets meet at a point a little up and left of its center: the top facet pale cream, the left warm peach, the bottom a hue-shifted rose, the one against the lips a deep magenta. Each carries the same small light inset triangle the skin facets have, and the two thin dark lines go. Why DMT: the face becomes one continuous jewel from the skin through the snout into the gem lips, so the mouth that sings the glyphs is a crystal too. Right now it is the one surface that looks like it came from the ordinary world.

The three hexagon third eyes on the skin (on the crest at about 420,255, by the dorsal fin at about 297,314, mid-body at about 366,382): I see them sinking into the curve of the sphere instead of floating on top of it. Squash each along the line from the ball's center (about 397,393) through the eye, more the nearer it sits to the edge: the crest one to about 65% along that line, the dorsal one to about 70%, the mid-body one to about 95%. A rotate(θ) scale(k,1) rotate(-θ) around each eye's center does it. Why DMT: the skin bends space around its eyes, so the ball reads as a true hyperdimensional polyhedron with eyes grown into its curved surface instead of badges pinned on. The portal eye stays round and frontal, and that makes it jump forward as the one eye that faces you head-on.
visions.keep: The tail tracers now sit clear of the fan with a gap you can see, so they read as motion, not as outline. Keep them, along with the facet ripple rolling out from the eye, the Necker-flipped corner rings, the Droste pupil with the fish at its bottom, the pupils turned toward it, the faint star net and the glyph curl from the lips. Keep the SAVES / FISH split capitals on their calm navy cartouches with nothing touching them. Keep the ultraviolet-to-gold countershading, the cream and gold crown on saturated cyan, the orb at three scales, and the chrysanthemum of eyed lancets and alien-faced gems.
